plainTitle: A study of ways to speed up the College streetcar

sources.label: Motion to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee from the Ward 11 Councillor

whatIsProposed.text: The committee asked City transportation staff and the TTC to study how to make the College streetcar faster and more reliable.

citations.quote: with recommendations how to improve the speed and reliability of the College Streetcar through transit priority measures that are within the control of the city

whatIsProposed.text: The study is about "transit priority measures". Examples given are changes to traffic signals and limits on parking and turns.
whatIsProposed.caveat: These examples come from the motion's summary. The decision itself does not name any specific measure for College Street.

citations.quote: Transit priority measures (including signal changes, and parking and turn restrictions)

whatIsProposed.text: Staff and the TTC are asked to consult the community as part of this work. The decision asks for a study only. It does not change any road rules now.

citations.quote: to consult the community and to report back to Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the first quarter of 2027

why.text: The motion says more than half of Ward 11 residents do not have a car and rely on transit, walking or cycling.

citations.quote: More than half of Ward 11 residents do not have private vehicles and depend on transit and active transportation.

why.text: The motion says Toronto streetcars are slow mainly because they get stuck in regular traffic.
why.caveat: This is the motion's summary of outside research. The record does not include that research.

citations.quote: due primarily to the vehicles being stuck in mixed traffic and lacking appropriate transit priority

why.text: The motion points to similar measures on Spadina, Bathurst and Dundas as showing that big improvements are possible.

citations.quote: that have been rolled out on Spadina, Bathurst and Dundas have demonstrated that considerable improvements are possible when transit gets the priority it deserves

whoIsAffected.text: People who ride the College streetcar.

citations.quote: improve the speed and reliability of the College Streetcar

whoIsAffected.text: People who drive, park, make deliveries or run a business on College Street could be affected later if parking or turning rules change.
whoIsAffected.caveat: The record does not say which blocks or which rules could change. That would come after the study.

citations.quote: Now it’s time to learn what is possible and achievable on College Street.

whoIsAffected.text: The City lists one ward for this item: 11 (University-Rosedale).

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The study only covers measures that the City itself controls.

citations.quote: transit priority measures that are within the control of the city

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: One committee member declared a conflict of interest and was absent from the votes.

citations.quote: The following member(s) declared an interest:

committee.text: The Infrastructure and Environment Committee adopted the motion without changes. The vote was 5 to 0.

citations.quote: This item was considered by Infrastructure and Environment Committee on July 15, 2026 and was adopted without amendment.

whatHappensNext.text: Staff and the TTC are due to report back to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the first three months of 2027, with recommendations.
whatHappensNext.caveat: No meeting date for that report is in the record yet. When it is scheduled, the City's page for that new item will show whether you can comment or speak.

citations.quote: to report back to Infrastructure and Environment Committee in the first quarter of 2027

location.label: College Street in Ward 11, from Yonge Street west to about 801 College Street
